fact_text: The State Bank of Pakistan kept its policy rate unchanged at 11% at the June 2025 meeting, the final monetary policy meeting of FY25, as widely expected.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: The policy rate was cut from 22% to 11% between June 2024 and June 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Brent crude rose from about $65 to above $75 a barrel after a geopolitical flare-up, and had eased to about $74 by the interview.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Inflation was about 3.5% in May 2025, which Frame Ventures CIO Shahbaz Ashraf described as the bottom of the cycle.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Ashraf expected FY25 average inflation of about 4.7%, and said inflation could rise again and go above the State Bank's target.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Pakistan's current account was expected to close FY25 in surplus, the first surplus in 14 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Financial account flows were negative over the four or five months before June 2025, and multilateral, bilateral and commercial inflows came in below expectations.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: SBP foreign exchange reserves were $11.7 billion, short of the $14 billion level the SBP had targeted.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: About $2.3 billion of inflows from ICBC, the World Bank, other multilateral lenders and commercial sources is needed to reach the $14 billion reserves target.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: The government's FY26 import target of $65 billion is needed to reach 4.2% GDP growth, up from a $60 billion import target.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: The 4.2% FY26 GDP growth target was called optimistic, against an average GDP target of about 1.7% over the three years to June 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: FY25 GDP growth of 2.7% was described as achievable but full of question marks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: The primary fiscal surplus was expected to close FY25 at about 2%, up from about 1% a year earlier, as the government moves toward fiscal consolidation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: The FY26 revenue target is about 18% higher than the prior year's, and the budget includes Rs312 billion of new taxes.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Enforcement of tax laws is expected to raise an extra Rs400 billion, which Ashraf called a little optimistic.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Agriculture grew 6.1% in FY24 and was expected to close FY25 near 6%, but Ashraf said the FY26 agriculture target of about 4% is uncertain.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Wheat, maize, sugarcane and rice output were all declining in 2025, according to Ashraf.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Ashraf argued monetary easing must be synchronised with fiscal policy, since tight fiscal policy limits how far growth can be pushed if rates fall further.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Ashraf said higher growth in a consumer- and import-driven economy raises imports, which puts pressure on FX reserves and the rupee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)

fact_text: Ashraf said a single-digit policy rate is more psychological than economically significant, and that the next steps depend more on fiscal policy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why SBP Kept Interest Rates Unchanged in June 2025 | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-06-16)
